messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 19
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: North American
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Fast Food Worker
  trauma_type: Natural disaster
  pcl5: 40

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Rehearse Conversations: rehearse what to say before any interaction, Avoid Stressors: avoid anything that could be stressful, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma
  Memory: Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time, Olfactory Recall: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened., Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
  Negative Appraisals: Unrecognisable Self: The person I have become is unrecognisable to me, Lost Happiness: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable., Permanent Damage: I have permanently changed for the worse

Vignette:
Tyler had always been a social and outgoing young man. But after experiencing the traumatic event of a devastating tornado that ripped through his hometown, he became unrecognizable to himself. The day started like any other, but by evening, the sky darkened ominously as wind picked up violently outside the fast food restaurant where Tyler worked. Panic set in when the manager announced they needed to take shelter. Tyler and his coworkers rushed into a small storeroom with reinforced walls, huddled together for safety. The sounds of shattering glass, howling winds, and debris slamming against the building were overwhelming. He could smell the acrid scent of burning wood and the metallic tang of rainwater mixed with dust. Despite their best efforts to stay calm, Tyler felt a wave of terror wash over him as the storeroom shook violently. In the days that followed, memories of the tornado haunted Tyler. Every time he thought about that day, he could smell the same acrid scent and see vivid images of the chaos outside the storeroom. These memories brought back the intense terror he felt during the event itself. He started to rehearse conversations before any interaction with coworkers or customers to avoid feeling anxious. Any stressful situation triggered his anxiety, so Tyler began avoiding anything that could potentially be distressing. The changes in Tyler were evident at work and in his personal life. His usual enthusiasm for socializing was gone; he would suppress thoughts of the tornado whenever they surfaced, often finding himself withdrawing from conversations with coworkers. This behavior strained his relationships with those around him, including a close friend who had been supportive but began to feel increasingly distant as Tyler pulled away. Tyler’s once vibrant personality transformed into one marked by constant misery and fear. He felt unrecognizable to the person he used to be, believing that he had permanently changed for the worse. His work performance suffered; he found it difficult to concentrate on his tasks, often becoming preoccupied with intrusive memories of the tornado during his shifts. The cumulative effect of these changes led to a noticeable decline in Tyler’s overall well-being. He struggled with maintaining basic daily routines and found himself increasingly isolated from others. It was his friend who finally urged him to seek help when they noticed how much Tyler had withdrawn and changed since the traumatic event. What frightened Tyler most was the idea that he would never be able to regain the person he used to be. Despite these fears, there was a glimmer of hope; he recognized that something needed to change in order for him to reclaim his life. Seeking help felt like a small step toward regaining control and rediscovering the happiness he once knew. Tyler’s current state reflects a young man grappling with profound changes brought about by trauma. He is determined to find a way through this dark period, hoping to emerge stronger on the other side.
